editorial: The search for authentic genius becomes a deeply uncomfortable family séance in this sophisticated drama. You will find yourself wrestling with the ethical abyss between creation and commerce as the plot explores what happens when art itself becomes a commodity. While the film’s commitment to mood can make the opening act feel overly languid, the precision of the final forgery sequence is genuinely thrilling. Ultimately, this meditation on legacy and ownership proves deeply affecting, offering a sophisticated, unsettling look at what it means to live in the shadow of artistic greatness.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy examining the tension between talent and emotional connection.
similarMovies: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
